+`Builder` is the existing core object, not a wrapper or a one-shot build function. Its API and `PreparedIndexes` live in `index_builder.go`. `NewBuilder` validates/defaults build settings without Kafka; `Service` keeps using `newIndexBuilder` with already-validated settings and shared metrics. Each object is single-cycle: call `ProcessStream` repeatedly, then `Prepare`, `PreparedIndexes.Upload`, and `Clear`. Pass `RecordRef{}` without Kafka context. Serialize ingestion, preparation, cleanup, and uploads externally; concurrent upload calls are serialized internally across prepared-value copies. The caller owns any asynchronous flush goroutine and store polling. The builder owns prepared file handles and scratch: uploads can be retried until `Clear` or the next `Prepare` attempt, which invalidates the previous result. Never process more streams after preparing or reuse a cleared builder. Both API and service uploads use the same uploader in `upload.go`.

Ingest appends `(ngram [8]byte, docID uint32)` pairs into ONE flat SoA buffer (`postingsBuffer`). `docID` is an **epoch tick**: `absCell - epochCell`, document cells counted from the FIXED `docIDEpoch` — 2026-01-01T00:00Z, the earliest Grafana Adaptive Logs Archive date, which Archive/Replay can legitimately replay, so the epoch must never move past it (a per-cycle derived epoch of now − 365d was tried and reverted for exactly that reason; `docid_window.go`). A cell is one `document_interval` bucket of one **document shard**: `absCell = absBucket << document_shard_bits | documentShard`, where the document shard is the top `document_shard_bits` bits of the stream's ingester fingerprint (`logline.DocumentShard`, hashed once per stream in `streamIngester.documentShard`). Document shards are v5 only and unrelated to `shard_count`, which splits files by n-gram; v3/v4 ignore `document_shard_bits` (0), so a cell is a bucket. All docID/date/doc-metadata math is in absolute cells (baseCell + tick), so `.lidx` output is epoch-invariant. A document's bounds are its bucket's, so cells of one bucket in different document shards share bounds. The epoch's midnight-UTC alignment keeps the epoch cell an exact multiple of `cellsPerDay`, which the merge's day/date math relies on. Date and shard are both recoverable from the pair itself, so all (date, shard) bucketing is deferred to flush. On buffer fill (`postings_buffer_pairs` pairs, default 20M) the fresh tail is radix-sorted, deduped, and 2-way merged into a sorted head ("incremental fill"); when the deduped head crosses the spill watermark (`postings_spill_watermark`, default 0.70), it is spilled to scratch disk as a sorted **run** (shard-contiguous records, one independently seekable s2 stream per shard — see `run_file.go`). At flush (`prepareIndexes`), runs are k-way merged into per-(date,shard) `.lidx` files (`merge.go`). `merge_threads` (default 1) bounds how many shards run at once; 1 is serial `mergeShard`. The cap is the shard count (`shard_count` 0 or 1 is one shard) because extra threads cannot overlap work. For v3/v4, referenced-tick bitsets per (shard, day) (`refTicks`, recorded at spill) seed each writer's document metadata and the epoch-tick-docID → dense-rank remap. v5 files have no document table and track no `refTicks` (`postingsBufferConfig.trackDocumentTicks`): postings hold cells of the file's day, `baseCell + tick − day × cellsPerDay`, and each writer gets that day's midnight as `WriterConfig.DayStart`. The fixed epoch is unchanged; only the merge output is day-relative.

If any step fails, retry that step (unbounded, with backoff). Never skip ahead. Never clear without committing. Known gap: `prepareIndexes` re-reads scratch runs, so a truncated/corrupt run fails identically on every attempt and the flush goroutine retries forever (and, via backpressure, eventually stalls the poll loop) until the pod is restarted — no data loss, but no forward progress. Fail-fast handling (bounded prepare retries → self-healing restart) is a backlog item.

-`prepareIndexes` writes `.lidx` files but does NOT delete run files. If an upload fails and the flush is retried, `finish()` is idempotent (buffer already drained ⇒ no-op) and the merge re-reads the surviving runs, reproducing the same file set. On merge failure, every `.lidx` written that attempt is removed and the runs are preserved: the failed shard cancels shards not yet started (in-flight siblings finish), `mergeShard` removes its own files, and `mergeRuns` removes those of shards that completed — files not yet returned to the builder, so invisible to `discardIndexes`. `discardIndexes` covers files already registered. Runs are deleted only by `clear()`, after every upload in the cycle succeeds.

### 7. docID window: out-of-window timestamps PANIC (deliberate never-panic override)

-`processStream` panics (`panicOutOfWindow`) on any timestamp outside the docID window: before `docIDEpoch` (2026-01-01T00:00Z) or at/past epoch + 2^32 cells, which is 2^(32 − `document_shard_bits`) × `document_interval` (2094-01-19T03:14:08Z at the v5 default of 16s × 2^5, 2039-08-12T00:38:49.6Z at 100ms time-only — pinned by `TestDocIDWindowEnd`; keep every documented window-end date in sync with it). This deliberately overrides the repo-wide "never panic" rule, documented here and at the panic site. Why: Grafana Adaptive Logs Archive/Replay can legitimately replay logs as old as 2026-01-01, and dropping an out-of-window line while the zero-file flush path commits Kafka offsets (invariant #1) would be a permanent, silent data skip; wrapping the tick would silently index the line under a wrong — possibly recent — date. A loud crash forces the anomaly (pre-epoch archive data, absurd future timestamp, misconfigured interval) to be dealt with. The panic message carries the offending record's partition/offset/tenant (`recordRef`, threaded through `processStream` and read only on the panic path) so remediation can target the poison record.

-**Drain-barrier invariant.** `prepareIndexes` on a (retired) pipeline builder first closes the queue, waits for every worker to finish in-flight items and exit, and surfaces the first worker error — only then does it `finish()` every buffer, so the zero-files ⇒ zero-pairs sub-invariant of invariant #1 still holds. After the barrier it OR-unions refTicks into the merge host, min/max-unions dateRanges, and merges the run union; all three are idempotent so retried prepares are safe. A worker spill error latches: subsequent enqueues fail fast through `processStream` (fails `running()`, pod restarts — identical failure surface to a serial spill error), and the barrier refuses the flush so pairs lost by the failed worker can never have their offsets committed. `clear()` re-runs the barrier as a backstop, so no worker goroutine outlives its builder even on abandoned flushes.
